<details class="how-to-read">
<summary>How to read this document</summary>

Small snippets of code are shown in a grey box like this:

```{.r}
cat("Hello!")
```

When the code is run, its output is shown below it, marked with a vertical red line:

```{r}
cat("Hello!")
```

Larger pieces of code are shown as scripts with a filename:

```{.r filename="script.R"}
name <- "Jean Golding"
cat("Hello,", name, "!")
```

Commands to run in a terminal look like this:

```{.bash filename="Terminal/Command Prompt"}
Rscript script.R
```

At the end of each section there is an exercise. Exercises are shown in blue boxes, followed by a yellow box that contains the answer. Try each exercise yourself before looking at the answer.

:::

This is the answer.
:::

Important points are highlighted in green boxes like this one:

::: {#keypointsN .callout-tip icon=false title='Key points'}
These are important concepts and technical notes.
:::

# First section

Each section opens with the question it answers.

## A first example

Code chunks are run when the notes are rendered, and their output appears underneath:

```{r}
heights <- c(1.62, 1.75, 1.80, 1.68)
mean(heights)
```

## Plots

Figures produced by code are embedded in the page:

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Histogram of eruption durations of the Old Faithful geyser"
hist(
  faithful$eruptions,
  main = "Old Faithful eruptions",
  xlab = "Duration (minutes)"
)
```

## Deliberate errors

Errors are shown in the notes rather than stopping the render. Mark chunks that fail on purpose with `#| purl: false`, so a script extracted with `knitr::purl()` still runs from top to bottom:

```{r}
#| purl: false
mean(heights_typo)
```

::: {#exercise1 .callout-note icon=false title='Exercise'}
Calculate the median of `heights`.
:::

::: {#answer1 .callout-caution icon=false title='Answer' collapse="true"}
```{r}
median(heights)
```
:::
